schema.purpose: Real Civilization VI game facts and historical background for each leader, rendered as the Civilization VI Profile section at the top of each generated guide.
schema.expansion_origin: Which Civ VI release introduced this leader/civ: Base Game | Rise and Fall | Gathering Storm | New Frontier Pass (Leader Pass persona). Where a leader is a same-civilization alternate persona layered on later DLC (e.g. Yongle/Tokugawa alongside Qin Shi Huang/Hojo Tokimune, or Age of Steam Victoria alongside the original Pax Britannica Victoria), that is noted in the leader_ability or historical_background text.
schema.leader_ability: The leader-specific ability, distinct from the civilization ability. name + a plain-English strategic summary.
schema.agenda: The leader's AI personality driver: what pleases or angers them in diplomacy.
schema.civ_ability: The passive ability every player of this civilization gets regardless of leader.
schema.unique_units: All unique units for the civilization (not leader-specific), with the unit they replace and why it matters.
schema.unique_infrastructure: All unique buildings/districts/improvements for the civilization, with type and why it matters.
schema.historical_background: Real-world historical context on the figure/civilization for strategic and flavor reference.

leaders.name: Gilgamesh

leader_ability.name: Adventures of Enkidu
leader_ability.text: When Gilgamesh declares war on a civilization that is already at war with one of his Allies, he suffers no warmonger penalty for it, and his units share pillage rewards and combat experience with the nearest allied unit within a few tiles. This rewards Gilgamesh for piling onto wars his allies have already started rather than starting his own.

agenda.name: Ally of Enkidu
agenda.text: Gilgamesh wants to form long-term Alliances and likes leaders willing to ally with him. He dislikes anyone who denounces or attacks his friends and allies.

civ_ability.name: Epic Quest
civ_ability.text: Sumeria receives a free Tribal Village-style reward each time it captures a Barbarian Outpost, and the Gold cost to levy military units from city-states is halved, making early aggressive expansion and city-state levying unusually cheap.

unique_units.name: War-Cart
unique_units.notes: An early ranged unit that hits harder than the standard Chariot Archer, letting Sumeria punch above its weight in the Ancient era.

unique_infrastructure.name: Ziggurat
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement that boosts Science and Faith, rewarding Sumeria for building tall with strong early yields outside of districts.

leaders.historical_background: Gilgamesh was the legendary king of the Sumerian city-state of Uruk, likely based on a real ruler from around 2700 BCE, and is the hero of the Epic of Gilgamesh, one of the oldest surviving works of literature. The epic recounts his friendship with the wild man Enkidu, their shared adventures and battles against monsters, and Gilgamesh's grief-driven quest for immortality after Enkidu's death. That central friendship is directly reflected in his Civ VI leader ability, Adventures of Enkidu, which rewards fighting alongside allies rather than alone. Uruk itself was one of the world's first true cities, and Gilgamesh was famed for building its great walls.

leaders.name: Amanitore

leader_ability.name: Kandake of Meroë
leader_ability.text: Cities gain a solid Production bonus toward Districts, which increases further in cities where a Nubian Pyramid is adjacent to the City Center, pushing Nubia toward rapid, district-heavy cities.

agenda.name: City Planner
agenda.text: Amanitore tries to build as many districts as possible in her cities and favors other leaders who also prioritize dense district development.

civ_ability.name: Ta-Seti
civ_ability.text: Nubia gets extra Production toward Ranged units, and those units earn combat experience faster than normal. Mines also yield bonus Production on strategic resources and bonus Gold on luxury resources, tying the civilization's military and economic strength together.

unique_units.name: Pitati Archer
unique_units.notes: A stronger, faster Ancient-era ranged unit that synergizes with Nubia's Ranged-unit production and experience bonuses for early ranged-rush strategies.

unique_infrastructure.name: Nubian Pyramid
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement (unlocked with Masonry) that generates Faith and gains extra yields when placed next to the City Center or other districts, rewarding compact, district-rich cities.

leaders.historical_background: Amanitore was a Kandake (ruling queen) of the Kingdom of Kush, centered at Meroë in what is now Sudan, reigning in the 1st century CE alongside her co-ruler Natakamani. Nubian kandakes held real political and sometimes military authority, a tradition distinct from many neighboring cultures, and several are remembered leading armies in defense of their kingdom. Amanitore and Natakamani presided over an extensive building program, constructing and restoring temples and pyramids at Meroë, Naqa, and elsewhere, which is echoed in-game by the civilization's pyramid improvement and its strong bias toward dense urban district construction.

leaders.name: Montezuma

leader_ability.name: Gifts for the Tlatoani
leader_ability.text: Luxury resources improved in Aztec territory grant an Amenity to two extra cities, and Montezuma's military (and religious) units gain Combat Strength on attack for each different luxury resource he has improved, making luxury acquisition a direct combat multiplier.

agenda.name: Tlatoani
agenda.text: Montezuma likes civilizations that possess the same luxury resources he does, and dislikes those who hold luxuries he lacks.

civ_ability.name: Legend of the Five Suns
civ_ability.text: Builders can be used to speed up (rush) the construction of Districts, letting the Aztecs convert worker labor directly into faster district growth.

unique_units.name: Eagle Warrior
unique_units.notes: A stronger melee unit than the standard Warrior that can capture defeated enemy units and turn them into Builders, fueling the civ's district-rushing ability.

unique_infrastructure.name: Tlachtli
unique_infrastructure.notes: Provides Faith, Culture, an Amenity from Entertainment, and Great General points, giving the Aztecs strong early culture and faith output from a military-adjacent building.

leaders.historical_background: Montezuma (Moctezuma II) was the ninth tlatoani (emperor) of the Aztec Empire, ruling from 1502 until 1520 at the height of its territorial power, commanding a tribute-based empire across central Mexico. He is best known historically for his fateful encounter with Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés in 1519, which set in motion the fall of Tenochtitlan and the Aztec Empire within two years. Aztec economic and religious life depended heavily on luxury goods and tribute, which is reflected in his in-game ability tying luxury resources directly to happiness and combat strength.

leaders.name: Tomyris

leader_ability.name: Killer of Cyrus
leader_ability.text: All of Tomyris's units gain a large Combat Strength bonus when attacking wounded (damaged) enemy units, and heal a significant amount of health whenever they eliminate a unit, rewarding aggressive follow-up strikes on weakened targets.

agenda.name: Backstab Averse
agenda.text: Tomyris favors leaders willing to become her Declared Friends, but strongly dislikes anyone who launches Surprise Wars, especially against a former friend or ally.

civ_ability.name: People of the Steppe
civ_ability.text: Training any light cavalry unit, or the unique Saka Horse Archer, produces two units for the price of one, giving Scythia an unmatched early-cavalry rush capability.

unique_units.name: Saka Horse Archer
unique_units.notes: A ranged cavalry unit that, combined with the civ ability, is produced in pairs, giving Scythia overwhelming early mounted numbers.

unique_infrastructure.name: Kurgan
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement built on flat land that generates Faith and Gold, giving Scythia useful yields even as a mobile, cavalry-focused civilization.

leaders.historical_background: Tomyris was queen of the Massagetae, a confederation of Iranian-Scythian nomadic peoples on the Central Asian steppe, in the 6th century BCE. She is remembered chiefly for defeating and killing Cyrus the Great of Persia in battle around 530 BCE after he invaded her territory, reportedly having his corpse's head placed in a wineskin filled with blood in retribution for her son's death at his hands. That victory over Cyrus is the direct namesake of her leader ability, Killer of Cyrus, and her agenda's suspicion of surprise wars mirrors the treachery she associated with the Persian invasion.

leaders.name: Simon Bolivar

leader_ability.name: Campaña Admirable
leader_ability.text: Whenever the game advances to a new era, Bolívar gains a Comandante General, a unique Great Person-style military leader whose presence heals and strengthens nearby Gran Colombian units, reinforcing sustained campaigns of conquest.

agenda.name: Carabobo
agenda.text: Bolívar respects leaders who build up large numbers of promoted, veteran military units, and favors civilizations that invest heavily in Encampments and unit experience.

civ_ability.name: Ejército Patriota
civ_ability.text: Gran Colombian units gain extra Movement and can be promoted without ending their turn, allowing units to level up and reposition in the same turn for highly mobile offensives.

unique_units.name: Llanero
unique_units.notes: Costs less to maintain, gains a combat bonus for each adjacent Llanero, and fully heals near an active Comandante General, rewarding massed cavalry pushes.

unique_infrastructure.name: Hacienda
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement unlocked with the Mercantilism civic that provides Production, Gold, and Housing, with extra Food for each adjacent Plantation, strengthening the economic base behind Gran Colombia's mobile armies.

leaders.historical_background: Simón Bolívar was the preeminent leader of the early 19th-century Spanish American wars of independence, liberating what are now Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Bolivia from Spanish colonial rule. Revered across Latin America as 'El Libertador,' he envisioned a unified South American state, Gran Colombia, which he helped found in 1819 but which fractured into separate nations shortly after his death in 1830. His campaigns depended on rapid, long-distance cavalry movement across difficult terrain, reflected in-game by his civilization's extra-movement and rapid-promotion abilities and the mobile Llanero cavalry unit named for the horsemen of the Venezuelan plains who formed the backbone of his armies.

leaders.name: Alexander

leader_ability.name: To the World's End
leader_ability.text: Removes war weariness in Alexander's cities, heals his units when he captures a city containing a Wonder, and unlocks his unique Hetairoi heavy cavalry unit, supporting a strategy of continuous, far-flung conquest without the usual unhappiness penalties.

agenda.name: Short Life of Glory
agenda.text: Alexander favors civilizations that are at war with someone other than himself and dislikes those at peace; in Gathering Storm, Grievances against him also decay twice as fast as normal.

civ_ability.name: Hellenistic Fusion
civ_ability.text: When Macedon captures a foreign city, it gains a bonus tied to the types of Districts already present there, letting Alexander's empire absorb and benefit from the specializations of conquered territory rather than razing them.

unique_units.name: Hetairoi
unique_units.notes: A powerful heavy cavalry unit unlocked by Alexander's leader ability, giving Macedon an early mounted strike force well ahead of other civilizations.

unique_units.name: Hypaspist
unique_units.notes: Gains a combat bonus when attacking districts and cities, making Macedon especially effective at siege and city capture.

unique_infrastructure.name: Basilikoi Paides
unique_infrastructure.replaces_note: replaces the Barracks, built in the Encampment district
unique_infrastructure.notes: Boosts Production, Housing, and combat experience for units trained in the city, and grants Science based on the cost of units produced, tying Macedon's military machine to both growth and research.

leaders.historical_background: Alexander the Great became king of Macedon in 336 BCE and, within thirteen years, conquered the entire Persian Empire, extending Macedonian rule from Greece to Egypt and northwest India before his death at age 32 in 323 BCE. His conquests spread Greek (Hellenistic) language, art, and institutions across the ancient world, blending with local cultures in the regions he took — the direct inspiration for Macedon's civ ability, which lets the empire absorb bonuses from captured cities rather than simply destroying them. After his death his generals, the Diadochi, carved his empire into rival successor kingdoms, and his relentless campaigning without ever losing a battle is echoed by his agenda's restless preference for a civilization always at war.

leaders.name: Gorgo

leader_ability.name: Thermopylae
leader_ability.text: Every combat victory grants Culture equal to a portion of the defeated unit's Combat Strength, turning Gorgo's wars into a steady source of Culture generation alongside conquest.

agenda.name: With Your Shield Or On It
agenda.text: Gorgo never yields territory or cities in a peace deal and admires leaders who likewise refuse to concede in negotiations; she dislikes anyone who has surrendered in a peace deal or who has never gone to war at all. In Gathering Storm, Grievances against her decay at twice the normal rate.

civ_ability.name: Plato's Republic
civ_ability.text: Greece gains an extra Wildcard policy slot in every government, giving it unmatched flexibility to mix and match policy cards regardless of which government is in use.

unique_units.name: Hoplite
unique_units.notes: Gains a large Combat Strength bonus when adjacent to another Hoplite, rewarding tightly packed phalanx-style formations reminiscent of Greek warfare.

unique_infrastructure.name: Acropolis
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique district (best placed on hills) that generates strong Culture output, reinforcing Greece's natural strength in a Culture Victory.

leaders.historical_background: Gorgo was queen of Sparta and wife of King Leonidas I, one of the few women of the ancient Greek world whose political wisdom and outspokenness were specifically recorded by the historian Herodotus. Leonidas famously led 300 Spartans (with allied Greek forces) in a last stand against the invading Persian army at the Battle of Thermopylae in 480 BCE, an event directly named in Gorgo's leader ability. Spartan culture prized unyielding martial resolve, epitomized by the (possibly apocryphal) saying attributed to Spartan mothers urging sons to return from battle 'with your shield, or on it' — the namesake of Gorgo's agenda, which rewards refusing to back down in war or negotiation.

leaders.name: Ambiorix

leader_ability.name: King of the Eburones
leader_ability.text: Training any non-civilian unit grants Ambiorix Culture equal to a share of that unit's Production cost, and his melee, anti-cavalry, and ranged units gain extra Combat Strength for each friendly combat unit adjacent to them, rewarding both militarization and massed unit stacks.

agenda.name: Scourge of Rome
agenda.text: Ambiorix admires leaders who maintain large military forces and looks down on those with few military units.

civ_ability.name: Hallstatt Culture
civ_ability.text: Mines grant an adjacency bonus to all districts along with bonus Culture, and can culture-bomb unowned territory into Gaul's borders; however, specialty districts cannot be built adjacent to the City Center and lose adjacency bonuses from other districts, pushing Gaulish cities to spread outward rather than stack districts centrally.

unique_units.name: Gaesatae
unique_units.notes: Costs more than a standard Warrior but hits far harder, especially against units with higher base strength and against district defenses, making it a potent early aggressive unit.

unique_infrastructure.name: Oppidum
unique_infrastructure.notes: Cheaper and available earlier than the Industrial Zone, defensible with its own ranged attack, and gains a strong adjacency bonus from Quarries and strategic resources, letting Gaul industrialize unusually early.

leaders.historical_background: Ambiorix was chieftain of the Eburones, a Belgic tribe in northeastern Gaul (modern Belgium), who led a major uprising against Julius Caesar's occupying Roman legions in 54 BCE, annihilating an entire Roman legion and inflicting one of Rome's worst defeats during the Gallic Wars. Caesar's brutal reprisal campaign nearly exterminated the Eburones, though Ambiorix himself reportedly escaped and vanished from history. He is remembered today, especially in Belgium, as an early symbol of resistance to Roman conquest, directly reflected in his in-game agenda 'Scourge of Rome' and his ability rewarding militarization and unit concentration reminiscent of guerrilla-style Gallic warfare.

leaders.name: Shaka

leader_ability.name: Amabutho
leader_ability.text: Allows the Zulus to form military units into Corps and Armies far earlier than other civilizations, unlocking these formations ahead of the normal Mercenaries and Nationalism civic requirements.

agenda.name: Horn, Chest, Loins
agenda.text: Shaka tries to organize as many of his units as possible into Corps and Armies, and dislikes civilizations that keep their military as unconsolidated single units.

civ_ability.name: Isibongo
civ_ability.text: Garrisoned units boost the Loyalty of their cities, and units automatically upgrade into Corps, Armies, Fleets, or Armadas upon capturing a city once the relevant civics are known, making Zulu conquest self-reinforcing.

unique_units.name: Impi
unique_units.notes: A cheap, low-maintenance Pikeman upgrade with a strong flanking bonus and faster experience gain, ideal for forming into Corps and Armies early.

unique_infrastructure.name: Ikanda
unique_infrastructure.notes: Built in half the normal time, letting the Zulu establish military infrastructure and start training Impi far earlier than rival civilizations.

leaders.historical_background: Shaka was king of the Zulu Kingdom in the early 19th century and one of the most transformative military leaders in southern African history, credited with reorganizing Zulu warfare around the short stabbing spear (iklwa), the 'buffalo horns' encirclement tactic, and age-grade regiments housed in fortified military kraals called amakhanda (singular ikanda) — the direct namesake of the civilization's unique district. His reforms fueled the Zulu Kingdom's rapid expansion and contributed to the wider upheaval and displacement across the region known as the Mfecane. His emphasis on organized, disciplined regiments is mirrored in-game by his leader ability's early access to Corps and Armies.

leaders.name: Cyrus

leader_ability.name: Fall of Babylon
leader_ability.text: For a number of turns after declaring a Surprise War, Cyrus's units gain bonus Movement and other yields, and cities he occupies with a garrisoned unit receive extra Loyalty, softening the usual drawbacks of launching a sudden attack.

agenda.name: Opportunist
agenda.text: Cyrus favors leaders who have themselves declared Surprise Wars and dislikes those who have never done so.

civ_ability.name: Satrapies
civ_ability.text: Persia gains a free Trade Route upon researching Political Philosophy, and its internal (domestic) Trade Routes generate enhanced yields, rewarding a strong internal trade network alongside military expansion.

unique_units.name: Immortal
unique_units.notes: Gains a bonus ranged attack and strong defense, making it unusually versatile compared to a standard melee Swordsman.

unique_infrastructure.name: Pairidaeza
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement ('paradise garden') that boosts Culture, Gold, and Appeal, with further bonuses based on adjacent districts, supporting a strong domestic economy.

leaders.historical_background: Cyrus II, known as Cyrus the Great, founded the Achaemenid Persian Empire in the mid-6th century BCE, rapidly conquering the Median, Lydian, and Neo-Babylonian empires (including the fall of Babylon referenced in his leader ability) to create the largest empire the world had yet seen. He was noted for relatively tolerant governance of conquered peoples, exemplified by the Cyrus Cylinder, and for a career built on swift, decisive military campaigns — reflected in his ability's rewards for surprise warfare. Cyrus was ultimately killed in 530 BCE in battle against Tomyris and the Massagetae, a fitting rival matchup within Civilization VI given her leader ability is literally named for his death.

leaders.name: Genghis Khan

leader_ability.name: Mongol Horde
leader_ability.text: All light and heavy cavalry units, plus the unique Keshig, gain bonus Combat Strength and a chance to capture defeated enemy cavalry units instead of destroying them, letting Genghis Khan's armies grow stronger the more they fight.

agenda.name: Horse Lord
agenda.text: Genghis Khan strives to build the world's strongest cavalry force and dislikes other civilizations that field powerful cavalry armies of their own.

civ_ability.name: Örtöö
civ_ability.text: Trade Routes to and from Mongolia instantly build a Trading Post in the destination city and grant an extra level of Diplomatic Visibility, echoing the historical Mongol relay-messenger and trade network.

unique_units.name: Keshig
unique_units.notes: A ranged cavalry unit unique to Mongolia that benefits from Genghis Khan's Combat Strength bonus on defense and can capture defeated enemy cavalry, reinforcing the civ's snowballing horde playstyle.

leaders.historical_background: Genghis Khan founded and became the first Great Khan of the Mongol Empire in the early 13th century, uniting the fractious tribes of the Central Asian steppe and forging, through his descendants, the largest contiguous land empire in world history. His success relied on highly mobile, disciplined cavalry armies, meritocratic promotion, and an extensive relay communication and trade network known as the Yam — the historical basis for Mongolia's Örtöö civilization ability. His campaigns were also marked by devastating psychological warfare and rapid conquest, a legacy echoed in-game by a leader ability that lets Mongol cavalry armies grow stronger by absorbing defeated enemy horsemen.

leaders.name: Chandragupta

leader_ability.name: Arthashastra
leader_ability.text: After researching Military Training, Chandragupta can declare a War of Territorial Expansion, granting his units extra Movement and Combat Strength for the following turns — a controlled way to seize nearby territory quickly.

agenda.name: Maurya Empire
agenda.text: Chandragupta seeks to expand his own empire and dislikes other civilizations that settle cities too close to his borders.

civ_ability.name: Dharma
civ_ability.text: Indian cities gain the Follower Beliefs of every religion present among their population, not just the majority religion. In Gathering Storm this also grants an Amenity for each religion with at least one follower and boosts Missionary spreads and Trade Route religious pressure, making India uniquely effective at multi-religion cities.

unique_units.name: Varu
unique_units.notes: An elephant-mounted heavy cavalry unit that causes nearby enemy units to become fearful (reducing their effectiveness) and resists the usual counters to cavalry, well-suited to India's defensive-leaning playstyle.

unique_infrastructure.name: Stepwell
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement that boosts Faith and Housing/growth-related yields, particularly valuable on dry terrain, supporting India's strong religious and population growth focus.

leaders.historical_background: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE, unifying most of the Indian subcontinent for the first time in history with guidance from his strategist advisor Chanakya, traditionally credited as author of the Arthashastra — the classical treatise on statecraft and military strategy directly named in Chandragupta's leader ability. His empire laid the foundation later expanded and famously ruled with a turn toward Buddhist pacifism by his grandson, Ashoka. India's long history as home to numerous major religions living alongside one another is reflected in the civ ability Dharma, which rewards accommodating multiple faiths within the same cities rather than enforcing religious uniformity.

leaders.name: Harald Hardrada

leader_ability.name: Thunderbolt of the North
leader_ability.text: Grants a large Production bonus toward naval melee units and enables coastal raiding (pillaging coastal tiles and cities directly from naval melee units), and unlocks the unique Viking Longship, supporting an aggressive naval-raiding playstyle. (Harald also has an alternate 'Varangian' persona, added later, with a different ability, Varangian Guard, focused on cheaply levying and maintaining city-state units.)

agenda.name: Last Viking King
agenda.text: Harald wants to build a powerful navy, respects other civilizations with strong naval forces, and looks down on those with weak ones.

civ_ability.name: Knarr
civ_ability.text: Norwegian units can cross Ocean tiles once Shipbuilding is researched, suffer no extra Movement cost for embarking or disembarking, and naval melee units can heal even in neutral (unowned) territory, giving Norway unmatched early naval mobility.

unique_units.name: Berserker
unique_units.notes: A strong early melee unit that gains a further boost once Military Tactics is researched, fitting Norway's aggressive coastal-raiding identity.

unique_units.name: Viking Longship
unique_units.notes: A cheaper, faster, and stronger early naval unit than the Galley it replaces, able to heal in neutral waters thanks to the Knarr civ ability, ideal for early raiding.

unique_infrastructure.name: Stave Church
unique_infrastructure.notes: Provides Faith and additional benefits, and in the Varangian persona also grants Influence points, supporting Norway's religious and diplomatic play alongside its raiding.

leaders.historical_background: Harald Hardrada ('Hard Ruler') was King of Norway from 1046 to 1066 and is often called the last great king of the Viking Age. Before taking the Norwegian throne he spent years as a mercenary commander in the Byzantine Empire's elite Varangian Guard, the historical basis for his alternate in-game persona. He died in 1066 at the Battle of Stamford Bridge in England while attempting to conquer the English throne, a defeat just weeks before the Norman Conquest that many historians treat as marking the symbolic end of the Viking Age — a fittingly aggressive, sea-borne legacy reflected in Norway's naval-raiding leader ability and civ-wide ocean mobility.

leaders.name: Matthias Corvinus

leader_ability.name: Raven King
leader_ability.text: Units levied from city-states gain bonus Movement and Combat Strength, cost far less Gold and resources to upgrade, and levying troops from a city-state grants 2 extra Envoys there, making city-state levying a core Hungarian military strategy.

agenda.name: Raven Banner
agenda.text: Matthias Corvinus frequently levies units from city-states and admires other leaders who do the same, while disliking those who avoid using mercenaries.

civ_ability.name: Pearl of the Danube
civ_ability.text: Districts and buildings built across a River from the City Center receive a large Production bonus, rewarding cities founded and developed along rivers.

unique_units.name: Black Army
unique_units.notes: An early professional-army unit that upgrades directly into Hungary's second unique unit, giving Hungary a long-lasting line of powerful cavalry-adjacent forces.

unique_units.name: Huszár
unique_units.notes: A strong light cavalry unit that continues Hungary's unique military line into the medieval era, well suited to levied-army compositions.

unique_infrastructure.name: Thermal Bath
unique_infrastructure.notes: Provides Amenities and helps prevent revolt/loyalty problems in newly conquered or levy-heavy cities, supporting Hungary's mercenary-driven playstyle.

leaders.historical_background: Matthias Corvinus ruled the Kingdom of Hungary from 1458 to 1490, nicknamed 'the Raven King' for his family's raven emblem (Corvinus), and is remembered as one of Renaissance Europe's most capable rulers. He built the Black Army of Hungary, one of Europe's first large professional standing armies, financed partly through mercenaries and levied forces, directly reflected in his in-game ability and agenda around cheaply levying city-state units. He also turned his court at Buda into a major center of Renaissance humanism, attracting scholars and artists from across Europe, and his Hungary sat astride the Danube, echoed by the civilization's river-adjacency production bonus.

leaders.name: Suleiman
leaders.leader_title: Suleiman I, The Magnificent (also known as Kanuni, "The Lawgiver")

leader_ability.name: Grand Vizier
leader_ability.text: Suleiman gains access to a unique, exclusive Governor (Ibrahim) with strong military and diplomatic bonuses, and unlocks the Janissary unique unit plus a bonus Governor Title once Gunpowder is researched. It lets the Ottomans field an elite late-game army while also running a top-tier governor for loyalty and diplomacy.

agenda.name: Lawgiver
agenda.text: Suleiman keeps his own cities happy and loyal, and is impressed by civilizations that do the same or have founded many cities; he dislikes leaders whose cities are unhappy, disloyal, or few in number due to conquest.

civ_ability.name: Great Turkish Bombard
civ_ability.text: Ottoman siege units are trained 50% faster and gain +5 Combat Strength when attacking or defending against district defenses, making the Ottomans exceptionally strong at both offensive sieges and city-state coercion.

unique_units.name: Janissary
unique_units.notes: Cheaper and stronger than the Musketman, starts with a free promotion, and can convert a defeated enemy unit into an Ottoman unit, letting Ottoman armies grow while attacking.

unique_infrastructure.name: Grand Bazaar
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Bank in the Commercial Hub, is the cheapest unique building in the game, and adds bonus Amenities and access to extra strategic resources.

leaders.historical_background: Suleiman I (r. 1520-1566) presided over the Ottoman Empire at its territorial and cultural zenith, pushing its borders deep into Hungary and the Middle East while his fleets contested the Mediterranean. Ottomans called him 'Kanuni' (the Lawgiver) for his sweeping legal and administrative reforms that brought consistency to a sprawling multiethnic empire, while Europeans knew him as 'the Magnificent' for his court's wealth and patronage of architecture (including the Süleymaniye Mosque) and the arts. His reign relied heavily on the elite, gunpowder-armed Janissary corps and an efficient siege-focused military, both reflected in the Ottomans' in-game strengths. This mix of centralizing governance and relentless military expansion is the throughline connecting the historical sultan to his in-game kit of governance-boosting abilities and siege-crushing bombards.

leaders.name: Lautaro

leader_ability.name: Swift Hawk
leader_ability.text: Defeating an enemy unit in enemy territory reduces the Loyalty of that unit's origin city, and Lautaro's units get a combat bonus when fighting civilizations that are in a Golden or Heroic Age, letting him punish and destabilize thriving rivals through raiding.

agenda.name: Spirit of Tucapel
agenda.text: Lautaro works to keep Loyalty high in his own cities and dislikes other civilizations that let their own cities' Loyalty slip, favoring stable, well-governed rivals.

civ_ability.name: Toqui
civ_ability.text: Cities with an established Governor gain bonus Culture, Production, and combat experience for trained units, and radiate Loyalty pressure toward nearby Mapuche cities, letting the Mapuche use Governors to both develop and hold their territory against Loyalty pressure.

unique_units.name: Malón Raider
unique_units.notes: A hard-hitting raiding cavalry unit that gains a combat bonus near friendly territory and can pillage for a single movement point, ideal for hit-and-run war-of-attrition strategies that punish rival Loyalty.

unique_infrastructure.name: Chemamull
unique_infrastructure.notes: A high-Appeal-requirement tile improvement that converts Appeal into Culture (and Tourism after Flight), making it a strong late-game culture/tourism engine for high-Appeal Mapuche territory.

leaders.historical_background: Lautaro was a young Mapuche man captured and pressed into service by Spanish conquistador Pedro de Valdivia in 16th-century Chile, during which time he learned Spanish cavalry and siege tactics from the inside. He escaped and used that knowledge to lead Mapuche forces in the Arauco War, most famously defeating and killing Valdivia at the Battle of Tucapel in 1553. His guerrilla-style raiding tactics and refusal to hold static ground helped the Mapuche resist full Spanish conquest for centuries, longer than almost any other indigenous American people, a legacy echoed in his in-game focus on mobile raiding and loyalty-destabilizing warfare against more 'settled' golden-age rivals.

leaders.name: Trajan

leader_ability.name: Trajan's Column
leader_ability.text: Every city Trajan founds or acquires gets an extra free building in its City Center slot beyond the normal one (a Monument if still in the Ancient Era, or the era-appropriate equivalent later), giving Rome a permanent head start on infrastructure in every city, new or old.

agenda.name: Optimus Princeps
agenda.text: Trajan tries to bring as much territory as possible under his empire's control and looks down on civilizations that hold only a small amount of territory.

civ_ability.name: All Roads Lead to Rome
civ_ability.text: All Roman cities start with a free Trading Post, roads are automatically built to new cities within trade range of the Capital, and Gold income from Trade Routes passing through Roman cities is increased, giving Rome an economic and connectivity edge from the earliest turns.

unique_units.name: Legion
unique_units.notes: A stronger, more expensive Classical-era melee unit that doesn't require Iron and carries a builder charge it can spend to construct a Roman Fort, build a road, or harvest a resource in the field.

unique_infrastructure.name: Bath
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Aqueduct (must be built adjacent to the City Center and a water/mountain feature) and provides Amenities alongside its Housing bonus, making Rome's early cities more comfortable to grow.

leaders.historical_background: Trajan ruled the Roman Empire from 98 to 117 AD and pushed it to its greatest territorial extent, conquering Dacia (for its gold) and campaigning into Mesopotamia and Armenia against Parthia. He is remembered as one of the 'Five Good Emperors' for combining military conquest with an ambitious building program: Trajan's Forum, Trajan's Market, and Trajan's Column (commemorating the Dacian Wars) all still stand in Rome today. His reputation for expanding territory while simultaneously building up infrastructure at home directly informs his in-game kit, which rewards both extra city buildings and holding maximal territory.

leaders.name: Hojo Tokimune

leader_ability.name: Divine Wind
leader_ability.text: Japanese land units get +5 Combat Strength on land tiles adjacent to Coast, and naval units get +5 Combat Strength in shallow water; Encampment, Holy Site, and Theater Square districts are also built in half the normal time, making Japan strong at coastal warfare and fast at fielding military/cultural/religious infrastructure.

agenda.name: Bushido
agenda.text: Tokimune favors civilizations that pair a strong military with high Faith and Culture output, and disapproves of civilizations that are militarily powerful but weak in Faith and Culture.

civ_ability.name: Meiji Restoration
civ_ability.text: Japanese districts receive the full (standard) adjacency bonus from being placed next to other districts, instead of the reduced 'minor' bonus other civilizations get, letting Japan pack districts tightly together for outsized yields.

unique_units.name: Samurai
unique_units.notes: A stronger Medieval-era melee unit that suffers no combat penalty when damaged, letting it keep fighting effectively even at low health.

unique_infrastructure.name: Electronics Factory
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Factory; a late-game production building that keeps Japan's tightly-packed district cities industrially competitive.

leaders.historical_background: Hojo Tokimune served as regent (shikken) of Japan's Kamakura shogunate from 1268 to 1284, a period defined by the Mongol Empire's two attempted invasions of Japan in 1274 and 1281. Tokimune organized Japan's samurai defenses and coastal fortifications to repel both invasions, and the second fleet was famously destroyed by a typhoon the Japanese called 'kamikaze,' or 'divine wind' -- the direct namesake of his in-game leader ability. A devout patron of Zen Buddhism, he is remembered as a symbol of samurai resolve and Japan's successful defense of its coastline, which the ability's coastal combat bonuses and fast military infrastructure evoke directly.

leaders.name: Qin Shi Huang

leader_ability.name: The First Emperor
leader_ability.text: Builders can be spent to instantly complete 15% of the original cost of Ancient and Classical era Wonders, and Builders gain an extra build charge, letting Qin Shi Huang rush out early Wonders far faster than other civilizations.

agenda.name: Wall of 10,000 Li
agenda.text: Qin Shi Huang likes civilizations that don't compete with him for Wonders and that build Wonders themselves; he strongly dislikes losing a Wonder race to another civilization.

civ_ability.name: Dynastic Cycle
civ_ability.text: Earning a Eureka or Inspiration grants an extra flat percentage of Science or Culture toward the associated Technology or Civic, and completing a Wonder grants a free Eureka and Inspiration, reinforcing China's wonder- and tech-rushing playstyle.

unique_units.name: Crouching Tiger
unique_units.notes: A cheaper ranged siege unit with strong ranged strength but shorter range than the Field Cannon it replaces, giving China an efficient siege option.

unique_infrastructure.name: Great Wall
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique defensive tile improvement that generates Gold (more when connected to adjacent wall segments) and grants a large defensive Combat Strength bonus to units standing on it.

leaders.historical_background: Qin Shi Huang unified China's warring states in 221 BCE to become its first emperor, founding the short-lived but transformative Qin dynasty. He standardized China's writing system, currency, weights and measures, and road networks, and connected and extended existing regional walls into the precursor of the Great Wall of China -- the direct basis for China's in-game unique improvement. He is equally famous for the enormous Terracotta Army buried to guard his tomb, and for a harsh, centralizing rule that built lasting state infrastructure at great human cost. His fixation on grand unifying construction projects and standardization is mirrored in his in-game ability to rush Wonders and China's civilization-wide bonus for converting breakthroughs into further progress.

leaders.name: Frederick Barbarossa

leader_ability.name: Holy Roman Emperor
leader_ability.text: Frederick gets an additional Military policy card slot and +7 Combat Strength when his units attack city-states, making him a formidable coercer and conqueror of city-states specifically.

agenda.name: Iron Crown
agenda.text: Frederick prefers civilizations that stay out of city-state affairs, and dislikes leaders who become suzerains of city-states or who conquer them.

civ_ability.name: Free Imperial Cities
civ_ability.text: German cities can build one additional District beyond what their Population would normally allow, letting Germany build wider, more district-dense cities than any other civilization.

unique_units.name: U-Boat
unique_units.notes: A cheaper Modern-era submarine with a combat bonus in ocean tiles and extra sight, giving Germany an efficient naval raiding tool.

unique_infrastructure.name: Hansa
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Industrial Zone; it gains adjacency bonuses from any resource (not just mines/quarries) and extra Production next to a Commercial Hub, making it a powerful, flexibly-placed production district.

leaders.historical_background: Frederick I 'Barbarossa' (red beard) ruled as Holy Roman Emperor from 1155 to 1190, spending much of his reign trying to reassert direct imperial authority over the fractious Italian city-states and princely territories that nominally owed him fealty -- a struggle his in-game agenda around city-states is built on. A leading figure of the Crusades, he drowned crossing a river in Anatolia while leading forces on the Third Crusade, and German legend later held that he was merely sleeping beneath a mountain, ready to return and restore Germany's greatness. That legacy of a fragmented Germany striving to hold its component territories together under central authority is echoed in the German civilization's extra-district ability, which lets Germany's cities exceed normal size limits the way the Holy Roman Empire itself sprawled beyond normal medieval state boundaries.

leaders.name: Pachacuti

leader_ability.name: Qhapaq Ñan
leader_ability.text: Domestic Trade Routes gain bonus Food for every Mountain tile near their origin city, and the Incas gain access to the Qhapaq Ñan unique tile improvement once the Foreign Trade civic is researched, rewarding mountain-heavy empires with strong internal trade.

agenda.name: Sapa Inca
agenda.text: Pachacuti wants to settle his own cities near Mountains and is happy to let other civilizations avoid that terrain, but dislikes rival leaders who also settle near Mountains and compete with him for that land.

civ_ability.name: Mit'a
civ_ability.text: Incan citizens can work Mountain tiles directly for Production (with an increased yield reached in the Industrial Era), and Mountains provide bonus Food to adjacent Terrace Farms, letting the Inca build thriving cities in terrain other civilizations must avoid.

unique_units.name: Warak'aq
unique_units.notes: A ranged unit with notably higher Ranged Strength than the Skirmisher it replaces, giving the Inca strong early ranged offense to complement their mountain-based defense.

unique_infrastructure.name: Terrace Farm
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique farm improvement buildable on hills/grassland/plains/desert that gets bonus Food next to Mountains and bonus Production next to an Aqueduct, letting mountain cities also feed themselves.

unique_infrastructure.name: Qhapaq Ñan
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique road-like mountain-tunnel improvement unlocked by Pachacuti's leader ability, granted automatically with Foreign Trade, that helps connect an Inca empire fragmented by mountainous terrain.

leaders.historical_background: Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui ruled from roughly 1438 to 1471 and is credited with transforming the small kingdom of Cusco into the vast Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu) through a combination of military conquest and sweeping administrative reform. He is traditionally credited with commissioning Machu Picchu and with building out the empire's remarkable road network, the Qhapaq Ñan, which linked its Andean territories across extremely difficult mountain terrain -- the direct namesake of his in-game leader ability and unique improvement. His empire's mastery of mountain agriculture, especially terrace farming, let the Inca feed large populations in terrain most other pre-modern states avoided, which is exactly what his in-game civilization ability rewards.

leaders.name: John Curtin
leaders.expansion_origin: Rise and Fall (Australia Civilization & Scenario Pack, a standalone DLC released alongside Rise and Fall, not part of New Frontier Pass)

leader_ability.name: Citadel of Civilization
leader_ability.text: Australia gains a large temporary Production bonus for a set number of turns after being on the receiving end of a Declaration of War, and an even longer-lasting Production bonus after liberating a captured city, letting Curtin turn being attacked (or liberating others) into a Production surge.

agenda.name: Perpetually on Guard
agenda.text: Curtin seeks Defensive Pacts with other civilizations and likes leaders who liberate captured cities, while disliking those who occupy and hold cities they've conquered.

civ_ability.name: Land Down Under
civ_ability.text: Coastal cities get bonus Housing, Pastures can trigger a Culture Bomb to claim surrounding territory, and Campus, Commercial Hub, Holy Site, and Theater Square districts get bonus yields on tiles with high Appeal, rewarding Australia for building scenic, coastal, well-developed cities.

unique_units.name: Digger
unique_units.notes: A stronger Modern-era infantry unit with combat bonuses on land tiles adjacent to water and when fighting outside Australian territory, fitting an expeditionary, coastal-defense playstyle.

unique_infrastructure.name: Outback Station
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement unlocked with Guilds (and upgradeable later) that develops otherwise marginal outback terrain, supporting Australia's wide, resource-heavy territory.

leaders.historical_background: John Curtin served as Australia's Prime Minister from 1941 to 1945, leading the country through the most direct existential threat it had faced: the Japanese advance through the Pacific during World War II, including air raids on Darwin and the fall of Singapore. Facing the limits of British support, Curtin controversially redirected Australian troops home from the Middle East and pivoted Australia's strategic alliance toward the United States, reshaping Australian foreign policy for the rest of the century. He died in office in July 1945, shortly before the war's end, worn down by the strain of wartime leadership. His defining legacy of turning a defensive crisis into national mobilization and a lasting policy of forming strong external alliances is reflected directly in his in-game kit's war-triggered production bonuses and preference for Defensive Pacts.

leaders.name: Victoria (Age of Steam)
leaders.leader_title: Queen of the United Kingdom (Age of Steam persona)

leader_ability.name: Age of Steam
leader_ability.text: Cities gain +10% Production for every Industrial Zone building present in them, and all Strategic Resources in England's territory (even unimproved ones) receive a flat Production bonus, making this Victoria persona a heavy Industrial-era production and Strategic Resource specialist rather than the original 'Pax Britannica' overseas-expansion leader.

agenda.name: Industrial Revolution
agenda.text: This Victoria persona pushes hard to build up industry and favors civilizations with high Production output, while looking down on those with low Production.

civ_ability.name: Workshop of the World
civ_ability.text: England gets bonus yields from Iron and Coal resources, greatly boosted Military Engineer production and extra Military Engineer charges, bonus yields from powered buildings, extra Production toward Industrial Zones, and increased strategic resource stockpiles from Harbors -- an Industrial-Revolution-themed civilization ability shared by all English leaders.

unique_units.name: Sea Dog
unique_units.notes: A unique naval raider that upgrades into the Submarine line and is strong at harassing enemy trade routes and coastal territory during the early-modern naval era; note the Redcoat unique unit is tied specifically to the alternate Victoria (Age of Empire) persona's leader ability, not to Age of Steam.

unique_infrastructure.name: Royal Navy Dockyard
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Harbor; grants a free naval unit when first built and extra Trade Route capacity/unit movement, reinforcing England's naval and trade-route strengths.

leaders.historical_background: Queen Victoria reigned over the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901, a period that saw Britain become the dominant global industrial and colonial power, with an empire famously described as one 'on which the sun never sets.' Her reign coincided with the height of the Industrial Revolution -- steam-powered railways, factories, and the Royal Navy's coal-fired fleet all expanded dramatically during this era, which is exactly what this 'Age of Steam' persona's Industrial Zone and Strategic Resource bonuses represent. This persona (added via the Leader Pass's Rulers of England content) is a deliberately narrower, industrially-focused counterpart to the original 'Age of Empire' Victoria persona, whose ability and Redcoat unit instead modeled 19th-century British colonial expansion overseas.

leaders.name: Ba Trieu
leaders.leader_title: Lady Trieu, folk heroine of Vietnamese resistance

leader_ability.name: Drive Out The Aggressors
leader_ability.text: Vietnamese units gain bonus Movement and Combat Strength while on Woods, Rainforest, or Marsh tiles, with the bonus doubled when those tiles are inside Vietnam's own territory, making Vietnam extremely strong at defending its jungle terrain against invasion.

agenda.name: Defender of the Homeland
agenda.text: Ba Trieu favors civilizations that have never declared war on Vietnam, and permanently distrusts and dislikes any civilization that ever has, regardless of how much time has passed.

civ_ability.name: Nine Dragon River Delta
civ_ability.text: Vietnam can only place specialty land districts on Woods, Rainforest, or Marsh tiles, but buildings in those districts gain bonus Culture, Science, or Production depending on the terrain feature, turning a placement restriction into a themed yield bonus.

unique_units.name: Voi Chiến
unique_units.notes: A Medieval ranged unit with more Movement and Sight than the Crossbowman, and the ability to move after attacking, well suited to Vietnam's mobile jungle-terrain warfare.

unique_infrastructure.name: Thành
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Encampment; provides bonus Culture for each adjacent district and, once Flight is researched, converts that Culture output into Tourism, giving Vietnam a militarized district with a late-game culture payoff.

leaders.historical_background: Triệu Thị Trinh, known as Bà Triệu ('Lady Trieu'), was a 3rd-century CE Vietnamese woman who led an armed rebellion against occupying Chinese (Eastern Wu) rule around 248 CE. Vietnamese tradition holds she declared she would rather 'ride the wind and walk the waves' and fight as a warrior than live bowed under foreign rule as a servant, and though her rebellion was ultimately crushed, she became -- alongside the earlier Trung Sisters -- one of Vietnam's most enduring symbols of resistance to foreign domination. That legacy of guerrilla resistance fought from Vietnam's dense terrain against a more powerful invader directly informs her in-game kit, which rewards fighting from (and defending) Vietnam's woods, rainforest, and marsh tiles and never forgives a civilization that has declared war on her.

leaders.name: Lady Six Sky

leader_ability.name: Ix Mutal Ajaw
leader_ability.text: Within 6 tiles of her Capital, all of Lady Six Sky's units get bonus Combat Strength and her cities get a yield bonus, but any of her cities founded more than 6 tiles from the Capital instead take a yield penalty, strongly rewarding a small, tightly-clustered empire over a sprawling one.

agenda.name: Solitary
agenda.text: Lady Six Sky wants to keep her own cities clustered close together near her Capital; she likes leaders who settle far away from her and dislikes those who encroach on her borders.

civ_ability.name: Mayab
civ_ability.text: Mayan cities don't get the normal Housing bonus from being adjacent to fresh water or Coast, but their Farms grant bonus Housing and Gold instead (with an added Production bonus next to an Observatory), letting the Maya build tall, food-driven cities away from rivers.

unique_units.name: Hul'che
unique_units.notes: An Ancient-era ranged unit with higher Ranged Strength than the Archer and a bonus against already-wounded units, giving the Maya strong early skirmishing power, especially near the Capital where Lady Six Sky's ability adds further Combat Strength.

unique_infrastructure.name: Observatory
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Campus; gets a major Science bonus from each adjacent Plantation and a minor bonus from adjacent Farms or districts, tying neatly into the Maya's farm-focused civilization ability.

leaders.historical_background: Lady Six Sky was a Maya queen who arrived at the city-state of Naranjo (in present-day Guatemala) around 682 CE and is credited with reviving it after a period of military defeat and decline, quite possibly having come from the powerful city of Dos Pilas or Calakmul. She oversaw military campaigns that restored Naranjo's regional power and, notably, placed her young son on the throne as king while continuing to wield significant authority herself, an unusual degree of female political power commemorated on Naranjo's carved stelae. That story of rebuilding and defending a single powerful city-state rather than pursuing distant conquest is mirrored directly in her in-game ability, which rewards a compact empire clustered tightly around the capital and penalizes overextension.

leaders.name: Nzinga Mbande

leader_ability.name: Queen of Ndongo and Matamba
leader_ability.text: All Kongolese cities on the same continent as the Capital (including the Capital itself) get a bonus to all yields, while any cities founded on other continents instead suffer a yield penalty, strongly pushing Nzinga toward staying concentrated on her home continent rather than overseas colonization.

agenda.name: Decolonization
agenda.text: Nzinga favors civilizations that have not settled any cities on her home continent, and dislikes those that have established a foothold there, reflecting her historical resistance to foreign colonization.

civ_ability.name: Nkisi
civ_ability.text: Kongo gets bonus Food, Production, Faith, and Gold from Relics, Artifacts, and Sculptures (including Heroic Relics), earns Great Artist, Great Musician, and Great Merchant points faster, and its Palace can hold extra Great Works, making Kongo a strong Culture/Great Works-focused civilization.

unique_units.name: Ngao Mbeba
unique_units.notes: A stronger melee unit that avoids movement/sight penalties in Woods and Rainforest and gets a defensive bonus against ranged attacks, well suited to fighting through and defending Kongo's forested homeland.

unique_infrastructure.name: Mbanza
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Neighborhood; unlocked earlier (with Guilds instead of Urbanization) and grants Housing, Food, and Gold, but can only be built on Woods or Rainforest tiles, matching Kongo's historical jungle-based settlements.

leaders.historical_background: Nzinga Mbande ruled the Central African kingdoms of Ndongo and later Matamba (in modern Angola) for roughly four decades in the 17th century, becoming one of the most formidable diplomats and military strategists to resist European colonization in her era. She skillfully played the Portuguese against rival African and Dutch powers, converted to Christianity as a political tool when useful, built alliances with escaped slaves and runaway soldiers to bolster her forces, and successfully kept her kingdoms independent of Portuguese control for most of her reign. Her lifelong struggle to keep foreign powers out of her home territory while she herself avoided overseas entanglement is the direct historical basis for her in-game ability and 'Decolonization' agenda, both of which reward staying concentrated on one's home continent and punish rivals who colonize it.

leaders.name: Seondeok

leader_ability.name: Hwarang
leader_ability.text: Each promotion a Governor has earned grants a percentage boost to both Culture and Science in the city they're assigned to, meaning heavily-promoted Governors turn into powerful Science and Culture engines under Seondeok.

agenda.name: Cheomseongdae
agenda.text: Seondeok focuses on maximizing her own empire's Science output and dislikes civilizations that produce comparatively little Science.

civ_ability.name: Three Kingdoms
civ_ability.text: Mines gain a Science yield and Farms gain a Food yield when placed adjacent to Korea's unique Seowon district, letting Korea weave its normal tile improvements directly into a Science-focused district strategy.

unique_units.name: Hwacha
unique_units.notes: A powerful Renaissance-era ranged siege unit that cannot move and attack in the same turn, trading mobility for strong ranged damage output.

unique_infrastructure.name: Seowon
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Campus and is Korea's central Science district, gaining adjacency bonuses from Mines and Farms placed near it rather than from the usual mountains/rainforest, tying directly into the Three Kingdoms civilization ability.

leaders.historical_background: Seondeok reigned as Queen of Silla, one of Korea's Three Kingdoms, from 632 to 647 CE, becoming the first reigning queen in Korean history. Her rule is remembered for its patronage of Buddhism, learning, and science, including the construction of Cheomseongdae, widely regarded as the oldest surviving astronomical observatory in East Asia and the direct namesake of her in-game agenda. She also strengthened Silla's diplomatic ties with Tang China during a period of intense rivalry among Korea's Three Kingdoms, groundwork that helped Silla eventually unify the peninsula after her reign. Her hallmark blend of scholarly patronage, astronomy, and governance is reflected in her in-game kit's emphasis on Science output and Governor-driven yield bonuses.

leaders.name: Hammurabi

leader_ability.name: Ninu Ilu Sirum
leader_ability.text: The first time each specialty district (except the Government Plaza) is constructed, Hammurabi instantly receives the lowest-production-cost building available for that district for free, plus a bonus Envoy for any other district built for the first time. This lets Babylon rush ahead on infrastructure and Eureka/Inspiration-style tech snowballing without spending production on the basic district buildings.

agenda.name: Cradle of Civilization
agenda.text: Hammurabi tries to build every possible type of district in his cities and respects civilizations that also pursue district variety; he looks down on civilizations that neglect districts.

civ_ability.name: Enuma Anu Enlil
civ_ability.text: Whenever Babylon triggers a Eureka or Inspiration, it can immediately unlock the full associated technology or civic by paying a share of its current per-turn Science or Culture output, letting a high-yield Babylon blitz through the tech/civic trees.

unique_units.name: Sabum Kibittum
unique_units.notes: An early melee unit with extra Movement and Sight and a large Combat Strength bonus against light and heavy cavalry, making it a strong early anti-horse defender.

unique_infrastructure.name: Palgum
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Water Mill; must be built in a city adjacent to a river, and adds Production, Housing, and extra Food from adjacent Freshwater tiles, reinforcing Babylon's strong early growth/science engine.

leaders.historical_background: Hammurabi (r. c. 1792-1750 BCE) was the sixth king of the First Babylonian Dynasty, who unified much of Mesopotamia under Babylonian rule through a mix of diplomacy and conquest. He is best remembered for the Code of Hammurabi, one of the earliest and most complete written legal codes, inscribed on a stone stele and organized into numbered provisions ('ninu ilu sirum' loosely 'when the exalted god...' opens its prologue) that lend their name to his in-game ability. His reign also oversaw major irrigation and building projects along the Euphrates, echoed in Babylon's river-and-floodplain-focused kit and its free-district-building leader ability.

leaders.name: Robert the Bruce

leader_ability.name: Bannockburn
leader_ability.text: Once Scotland researches the Defensive Tactics civic, Robert can declare a War of Liberation; doing so grants all his units +100% Production and +2 Movement for the following 10 turns, turning a defensive liberation war into a powerful offensive window.

agenda.name: Flower of Scotland
agenda.text: Robert will not attack civilizations that share a landmass with him unless they break a promise, and he dislikes leaders who attack their own neighbors unprovoked.

civ_ability.name: Scottish Enlightenment
civ_ability.text: Happy cities gain bonus Science and Production, plus extra Great Scientist points per Campus and Great Engineer points per Industrial Zone; Ecstatic cities double these bonuses, rewarding Scotland for maximizing city Amenities.

unique_units.name: Highlander
unique_units.notes: A Recon-class unit that fights especially well in Hills and Woods, well suited to Scotland's rugged, resource-rich terrain.

unique_infrastructure.name: Golf Course
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement that generates Amenities and Gold once built, rewarding Scotland's happiness-driven playstyle.

leaders.historical_background: Robert the Bruce (1274-1329) was King of Scots who led Scotland during the Wars of Scottish Independence against England. His decisive victory at the Battle of Bannockburn in 1314 secured effective Scottish independence and is the namesake of his signature in-game ability, which rewards declaring a liberating war. Earlier in his career he had also endured defeats and exile before rallying Scottish nobles to his cause, reflecting the game's framing of him as a defensive, promise-keeping leader who only turns aggressive when wronged.

leaders.name: Teddy Roosevelt (Bull Moose)

leader_ability.name: Antiquities and Parks (Bull Moose persona of Roosevelt Corollary)
leader_ability.text: The default (non-persona) Teddy Roosevelt's ability, Roosevelt Corollary, grants units +5 Combat Strength on his home continent and +1 Appeal to all tiles in any city containing a National Park. When Persona Packs are enabled, Roosevelt splits into two alternate personas: Rough Rider (keeps a Roosevelt Corollary variant focused on the home-continent combat bonus and doubled Envoys to trade-route city-states) and Bull Moose, whose ability 'Antiquities and Parks' instead grants bonus Science on tiles of Breathtaking Appeal adjacent to a Natural Wonder or Mountain, and bonus Culture on Breathtaking tiles adjacent to a Wonder or Woods — a peaceful, conservation-and-culture playstyle built around National Parks and high-Appeal terrain.

agenda.name: Big Stick Policy
agenda.text: Roosevelt (in both personas) likes peaceful civilizations that share his continent and dislikes any civilization that starts a war on that continent.

civ_ability.name: Founding Fathers
civ_ability.text: America's civilization ability has evolved across versions: in the base game it halved the time to earn government legacy bonuses; in Rise and Fall it instead converts all Diplomatic policy slots in the current government into Wildcard slots; Gathering Storm added +1 Diplomatic Favor per turn for each Wildcard slot in the current government, making America's policy setup unusually flexible.

unique_units.name: Rough Rider
unique_units.notes: An Industrial era heavy cavalry unit with a Combat Strength bonus on Hills and reduced maintenance, reflecting Roosevelt's historical cavalry regiment.

unique_units.name: P-51 Mustang
unique_units.notes: A Modern era air unit with bonus attack against other fighters, extra range, and faster experience gain, giving America strong air superiority in the late game.

unique_infrastructure.name: Film Studio
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Broadcast Center and adds extra Tourism pressure toward other civilizations in the Modern era, supporting a Culture/Tourism victory.

leaders.historical_background: Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt (1858-1919) was the 26th U.S. President, a Progressive-era reformer known for trust-busting, conservation of public lands, and an assertive foreign policy summarized by his phrase 'speak softly and carry a big stick' (the source of his in-game agenda name). After leaving the presidency he ran for a third term in 1912 as the candidate of the Progressive 'Bull Moose' Party, the persona referenced in this leader's parenthetical name, campaigning on social reform rather than the more militaristic image of his earlier 'Rough Rider' cavalry service in the Spanish-American War. His dual legacy as both war hero and national-parks conservationist is split directly into Civ VI's two Roosevelt personas.

leaders.name: Kupe

leader_ability.name: Kupe's Voyage
leader_ability.text: Kupe begins the game embarked on the Ocean rather than on land, earning +2 Science and +2 Culture per turn before he founds his first city. Founding that first city grants a free Builder and +1 Population, and his Palace provides extra Housing and an Amenity, smoothing the unusual late, ocean-based start.

agenda.name: Kaitiakitanga
agenda.text: Kupe preserves natural features and builds National Parks; he likes civilizations that respect the environment (avoiding harvesting and terrain removal) and dislikes those who despoil it.

civ_ability.name: Mana
civ_ability.text: The Māori start with Sailing and Shipbuilding and can move directly onto Ocean tiles from the outset. Their embarked units gain bonus Combat Strength and Movement, unimproved Woods and Rainforest tiles yield bonus Production, and Fishing Boats grant extra Food and trigger a Culture Bomb, making the Māori strong at settling and expanding across open ocean.

unique_units.name: Toa
unique_units.notes: A Classical era melee unit that can build the defensive Pā improvement on hills and weakens adjacent enemy units with a Haka war dance, giving the Māori solid mid-game defense despite their peaceful, exploration-focused kit.

unique_infrastructure.name: Marae
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Amphitheater in the Theater Square; it grants Culture and Faith from every passable feature (e.g., Woods, Floodplains) in the city and Tourism after Flight, rewarding a Māori empire that keeps its natural terrain intact.

leaders.historical_background: Kupe is a legendary Polynesian navigator credited in Māori oral tradition with being one of the first explorers to discover and name Aotearoa (New Zealand), guiding a great ocean-going waka (canoe) across the Pacific using wayfinding by stars, currents, and birds. As a figure of oral history rather than documented record, his exact dates are unknown, but he is central to Māori foundational narratives of migration and settlement. His in-game role as an ocean-starting leader who arrives to found cities directly mirrors this voyaging legend, and the Māori civilization's environmental, ocean-adjacency-focused kit reflects traditional Māori concepts of kaitiakitanga (guardianship of nature).

leaders.name: Pericles

leader_ability.name: Surrounded by Glory
leader_ability.text: Pericles gains bonus Culture for every city-state of which he is Suzerain, rewarding an aggressive envoy/diplomacy strategy aimed at accumulating city-state alliances.

agenda.name: Delian League
agenda.text: Pericles favors leaders who are not competing with him for the same city-states' suzerainty, and dislikes leaders who directly contest the city-state alliances he is pursuing.

civ_ability.name: Plato's Republic
civ_ability.text: Greece gains an extra Wildcard policy card slot in every government, giving it unusual flexibility to mix and match policy cards for whichever strategy (culture, science, or otherwise) it is pursuing.

unique_units.name: Hoplite
unique_units.notes: Gains a very large Combat Strength bonus when adjacent to another Hoplite, rewarding tight phalanx-style formations reminiscent of Greek warfare.

unique_infrastructure.name: Acropolis
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Theater Square, must be built on a Hill, and gets stronger Culture adjacency bonuses from neighboring districts (including the City Center), making Greek cities strong culture generators.

leaders.historical_background: Pericles (c. 495-429 BCE) was the leading statesman of Athens during its Golden Age, guiding the city through the height of its democratic institutions, its cultural flourishing (including the Parthenon and other Acropolis monuments, echoed by Greece's unique district), and the early years of the Peloponnesian War against Sparta. He was famously eulogized by Thucydides as effectively Athens' 'first citizen' despite holding no monarchical title, a nod reflected in his in-game leader title. His policy of forging and managing an alliance network among Greek city-states — the Delian League — is the direct inspiration for his in-game agenda's focus on city-state suzerainty.

leaders.name: Cleopatra (Ptolemaic)
leaders.expansion_origin: New Frontier Pass (Persona Packs) for the base 'Cleopatra' persona; Ptolemaic Cleopatra specifically is a Leader Pass persona (Rulers of the Sahara Pack)

leader_ability.name: Arrival of Hapi
leader_ability.text: As the Ptolemaic persona (added later via the Leader Pass' Rulers of the Sahara Pack), Cleopatra's ability grants resources on Floodplains +1 Food and +1 Culture, and Floodplains in her territory grant adjacent tiles +1 Appeal instead of the usual -1. (Her original, base-game persona instead uses the ability Mediterranean's Bride, which gives bonus Gold on Egypt's outgoing Trade Routes and bonus Food/Gold on incoming ones.)

agenda.name: Basilike Ge
agenda.text: As Ptolemaic Cleopatra, she favors civilizations with high Food output and dislikes those with low Food output. (Her original persona's agenda, Queen of the Nile, instead favors leaders with powerful militaries and dislikes weak ones.)

civ_ability.name: Iteru
civ_ability.text: Egypt builds Wonders and districts faster when adjacent to a river, and uniquely can construct Wonders and districts directly on Floodplains, letting Egypt turn its floodplain-heavy river valleys into dense wonder- and district-packed cities.

unique_units.name: Maryannu Chariot Archer
unique_units.notes: A fast Ancient era ranged cavalry unit with strong Ranged Strength and extra Movement on open terrain, giving Egypt an unusually powerful early rush/exploration unit.

unique_infrastructure.name: Sphinx
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement giving Faith and Culture (with a bonus when adjacent to a Wonder), and Tourism after Flight, reinforcing Egypt's wonder- and culture-focused playstyle.

leaders.historical_background: Cleopatra VII Thea Philopator (69-30 BCE) was the last active ruler of Egypt's Ptolemaic dynasty, a Greek Macedonian line established after Alexander the Great's conquests, ruling Egypt for nearly three centuries before Roman annexation. Fluent, politically astute, and famed for her alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony, she worked to preserve Egyptian independence against expanding Roman power, ultimately losing at the Battle of Actium. Civ VI splits her into two personas reflecting this hybrid identity: a base-game 'Egyptian' Cleopatra evoking the older pharaonic tradition and river/floodplain economy of the Nile, and a Leader Pass 'Ptolemaic' persona (Arrival of Hapi, named for the Egyptian god of the Nile flood) emphasizing her Hellenistic-Egyptian royal household and its farmland (basilike ge, 'royal land').

leaders.name: Pedro II

leader_ability.name: Magnanimous
leader_ability.text: Whenever Pedro recruits or patronizes a Great Person, he recoups a portion (about a fifth) of the Great Person points spent, letting Brazil chase Great People more efficiently and repeatedly.

agenda.name: Patron of the Arts
agenda.text: Pedro wants to acquire as many Great People as possible and dislikes civilizations that beat him to Great People he was pursuing.

civ_ability.name: Amazon
civ_ability.text: Rainforest tiles in Brazilian territory give +1 Appeal instead of the usual -1, and Rainforest provides the standard adjacency bonus to Campuses, Commercial Hubs, Holy Sites, and Theater Squares — turning Brazil's rainforest-heavy terrain from a liability into a major yield and Appeal asset.

unique_units.name: Minas Geraes
unique_units.notes: A powerful Modern era naval unit with strong Anti-Air and bombardment capability, reflecting the historical Brazilian dreadnought of the same name.

unique_infrastructure.name: Street Carnival
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Entertainment Complex and adds bonus Amenities and Culture/Tourism, letting Brazil generate happiness and tourism cheaply.

unique_infrastructure.name: Copacabana
unique_infrastructure.notes: A Rise and Fall unique improvement replacing the Water Park, giving bonus Appeal, Amenities, and Tourism along Brazil's coastlines.

leaders.historical_background: Dom Pedro II (1825-1891) ruled the Empire of Brazil for nearly 50 years, presiding over a long period of relative internal stability, gradual abolition of slavery, and active patronage of the sciences and arts (he corresponded with scientists worldwide and funded research and exhibitions), which inspires his in-game focus on collecting Great People. His reign ended with a bloodless 1889 military coup that established the Brazilian republic, after which he lived out his life in exile in Europe. Brazil's unusual rainforest-friendly civilization ability reflects the country's Amazonian geography, a defining feature of the empire he ruled.

leaders.name: Ludwig II
leaders.expansion_origin: New Frontier Pass / Leader Pass (Great Builders Pack persona)

leader_ability.name: Swan King
leader_ability.text: All Wonders (finished or still under construction) grant 2 Culture from each adjacent District, and after researching Castles, all Culture adjacency bonuses also generate Tourism — turning a wonder-dense empire into a strong late-game Culture/Tourism engine.

agenda.name: Eternal Enigma
agenda.text: Ludwig favors civilizations that do not max out the number of Districts in their cities, and dislikes those who pack their cities with as many Districts as possible.

civ_ability.name: Free Imperial Cities
civ_ability.text: German cities can build one additional District beyond what their Population would normally allow, letting Germany build wider, more specialized cities earlier than other civilizations.

unique_units.name: U-Boat
unique_units.notes: A stronger, stealthier submarine unit reflecting Germany's historical submarine warfare, useful for both raiding and area denial at sea.

unique_infrastructure.name: Hansa
unique_infrastructure.notes: Germany's unique Industrial Zone replacement: cheaper to build, with better adjacency bonuses (from Commercial Hubs and resources) for Production, making it easier to power through Ludwig's many Wonders.

leaders.historical_background: Ludwig II (1845-1886) was King of Bavaria, famous less for statecraft than for his extravagant, fairy-tale castle-building projects — most notably Neuschwanstein Castle — and his devoted patronage of composer Richard Wagner, which together earned him the nickname 'the Swan King,' the name of his in-game ability. His reign saw Bavaria's political independence curtailed as Germany unified under Prussian leadership, and he died in disputed circumstances shortly after being declared mentally unfit to rule. As a Leader Pass persona representing Germany despite historically ruling only Bavaria, his in-game focus on wonder-building and culture/tourism is a direct nod to his architectural obsessions.

leaders.name: Kristina

leader_ability.name: Minerva of the North
leader_ability.text: Any building with at least 3 Great Work slots and any Wonder with at least 2 Great Work slots is automatically 'themed' once all its slots are filled (no need to manually match eras/types), and Kristina can build the unique Queen's Bibliothèque in the Government Plaza — a 6-slot Great Work building (2 each for Writing, Art, and Music) that also grants Great Person points, a Governor Title, and a policy card, making Sweden extremely efficient at Culture Victory play.

agenda.name: Bibliophile
agenda.text: Kristina tries to collect as many Great Works as possible and likes leaders who leave Great Works for her to acquire; she dislikes rivals who compete hard for the same Great Works.

civ_ability.name: Nobel Prize
civ_ability.text: Sweden gains bonus Great Scientist and Great Engineer points from Universities and Factories, generates Diplomatic Favor for every Great Person it recruits, and unlocks three unique World Congress competitions from the Industrial era onward, blending science, culture, and diplomacy.

unique_units.name: Carolean
unique_units.notes: A Renaissance era unit with extra Movement and a Combat Strength bonus for each point of unused Movement, plus bonus strength against cavalry, rewarding aggressive, mobile play.

unique_infrastructure.name: Open-Air Museum
unique_infrastructure.notes: Grants Culture and Tourism scaling with the variety of terrain types (Snow, Tundra, Desert, Plains, Grassland) Swedish cities are founded on, up to one per city, rewarding geographically diverse settling.

leaders.historical_background: Kristina (1626-1689) was Queen of Sweden from 1632 to 1654, a famously erudite and unconventional monarch who turned Stockholm into a hub for scholars, philosophers (including René Descartes, who died there), and artists, earning Sweden the nickname 'Athens of the North' during her reign — the direct inspiration for her in-game 'Minerva of the North' ability and Great Works focus. She abdicated the throne in 1654, converted to Catholicism (a controversial act for a Lutheran monarch), and spent much of her later life in Rome as a patron of the arts and sciences. Her personal passion for collecting books, art, and manuscripts is reflected in Sweden's Great Works/Bibliophile-centered kit.

leaders.name: Catherine de Medici (Black Queen)
leaders.expansion_origin: Base Game (Black Queen is Catherine's original/default persona; the alternate 'Magnificence' persona was added later via New Frontier Pass Persona Packs)

leader_ability.name: Catherine's Flying Squadron
leader_ability.text: As the Black Queen persona (her default, original ability), Catherine gains one extra level of Diplomatic Visibility with every civilization she has met, receives a free Spy upon researching Castles, and all her Spies start with a free promotion — making her the strongest espionage leader in the game. (Her alternate Magnificence persona instead focuses on collecting and trading Luxury resources via the agenda 'Sumptuous Finery.')

agenda.name: Black Queen
agenda.text: Catherine wants to accumulate as many Spies and as much Diplomatic Visibility as possible, and dislikes leaders who ignore espionage entirely.

civ_ability.name: Grand Tour
civ_ability.text: France gets bonus Production toward Medieval, Renaissance, and Industrial era Wonders, and doubles the Tourism generated by Wonders of any era, making France one of the strongest wonder-rush/culture-victory civilizations.

unique_units.name: Garde Impériale
